# Draft:Anandeshwar Mandir, Lasur, Daryapur Amravati, Maharashtra

Anandeshwar Temple is an ancient temple of Siva with Circular Swarg Mandap similar to Kopeshwar, Khidrapur. Anandeshwar is on the bank of Purna river in Lasur village in Daryapur taluka in Amravati district on Paratwada Akola road, in Vidarbha region of Maharashtra.
Probably of the Chalukya period temple, Anandeshwar is very mystical in construction and does not follow either Dravidian/Chalukyan or Nagar style. However there is no concrete proof of it that it is of Chalu khan period. The wearing of the murtis on outer walls indicate at least of 1000 to 1200 years of age.
Temple has three independent blocks like leaves and they are connected in the middle by Circular open to sky Swarg Mandap. The main entrance is unusually towards North and pranala of Shivling in Sanctum is towards the entry.
Built on a hillock and appearing like a fortress, the temple is built on a raised big stone platform.
Temple has only one entry point. When you enter it, there is Swarg Mandap and on two sides are two domed temples. The idols of those two are missing. No one knows which deities resided there.
The outer wall is in Octagonal shape with many intricately carved murti, Vishnu Lakshmi, Nrusimha and Mahishasur mardini are specifically notable. Some sculptures are erotic and there is also a lady sculpture making up her lips.
Big stone blocks are used in interlocking method.
